approach.method_basis: The Parent samples local molecular graph edits from one scored current state, normalizes identities, rejects duplicates and sends the first full tabu-admissible batch for evaluation. It then walks to the best accepted neighbor, including worsening moves, while retaining an independent best archive. Bond changes alter bond order; deletions remove atoms or leaves. Neither directly relocates an intact side group along an aromatic ring. The Parent already includes the repaired identity join and its established inverse-motif memory.
approach.novelty: Add one intact-substituent relocation along an existing aromatic ring edge. Detach an acyclic pendant group from an aromatic carbon and reconnect the same group to an adjacent aromatic carbon bearing a hydrogen. This changes substitution position while retaining the whole group, the ring framework and molecular formula. The move becomes an extra choice when the existing bond-change operator selects that attachment bond. Earlier branch deletion discarded groups; nitrogen exchange moved ring elements. This experiment instead reconnects an existing side group and incorporates neither earlier extension.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-9f7c7ec50039 completes the supplied panel at mean 0.5209178281192797 and population standard deviation 0.004890242222897396, but its bond-change menu only changes bond order. It cannot directly move an attached substituent to a different ring position while retaining the substituent and the ring. The branch-deletion sibling n-0e56e71777c4 exposed compact alternatives but all three endpoint scores regressed; sampled deletions usually lost source score and the selected prunings were followed by regrowth. The nitrogen-exchange sibling n-abcd951ab7cc confirms that formula-preserving positional changes can be score-visible, yet only ten exchanges reached evaluation and its paired panel gain of 0.0008412882577690054 missed the 0.002 target. A separate offline audit of the Parent's 435 recorded batch starts finds intact acyclic branch relocation opportunities in 354 states: 1244 concrete source-attachment/adjacent-target edits, all valid, formula-preserving, equal in atom/bond counts and unchanged in aromatic atom count. All 1244 differ from their source; 1243 are then unseen, corresponding to 1123 distinct fresh products after deduplicating within each source state. Branch sizes range from one to ten atoms; 429 of 1244 options move more than one atom as an intact substituent. Among 741 recorded change_bond draws, 36 select an attachment bond that would gain such options. Actual Parent bond-order draws have 548 invalid/inapplicable outcomes, 190 emissions and three tabu vetoes. These recorded and unscored results establish a missing direct connectivity channel and exposure denominators, not that alternative attachment positions have better scores.
hypothesis: Extend the existing change_bond neighborhood with relocation of an intact single-attachment acyclic branch from an aromatic carbon to its adjacent hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon, directly exposing substitution-position isomers while preserving the branch, ring framework and molecular formula.

finding_summary.headline: Ten intact-group position changes were evaluated, but none carried the improved panel score
finding_summary.insights: Direct positional accessibility is established: none of the ten scored products is reachable by a single original bond-order change, and each changes local motifs and measured score. Intact-group retention therefore avoids the necessary atom loss of branch deletion, but it does not reliably make a stronger neighbor. All four evaluated larger-branch relocations lose to their sources, including the methoxy and carboxyl shifts. The distinction between a successful panel and useful new molecules matters here: since no relocation is selected, the panel gain cannot be credited to descendants carrying a moved group. The expanded menu also changes proposal choices and batch competition among the original operators. The evidence supports a working positional channel and one local thiol-position gain, while leaving a reproducible score benefit from retaining a new position unresolved. The stronger sulfur-free aryl-amine series identified by the molecular assessment is an original-operator outcome and still contains strained nitrogen rings; other populations retain unusual sulfur and reactive heteroatom bonds. Conserving the existing group and ring has not established better stability or synthetic accessibility.
finding_summary.results: Ten fresh positional isomers reached evaluation from thirteen sampled branch relocations, with all atoms, the complete branch, molecular formula and aromatic ring framework retained. Six moved one-heavy-atom groups and four moved larger groups. One thiol position change improved its source score; the other nine lost. None won its batch, updated the best archive or produced a later walk descendant. The three-seed macro mean nevertheless rose from 0.520918 to 0.525257, a paired gain of 0.004339 that exceeds the 0.002 target. One seed improved and two declined; the largest endpoint gain was in one DRD2 seed, while median_2 and sitagliptin endpoints were unchanged throughout.

molecular.headline: Sulfur-rich cages persist; a stronger aryl-amine family removes sulfur but retains strained nitrogen rings
molecular.overall_character: All supplied current and parent trajectories were inspected. Every objective has 900 entries, including 870 optimizer proposals, and none lacks trajectories. These are consistently substantial ring-containing molecules: ring-closure and branch presence rates are 1.0 throughout. Aromatic-token presence is also 1.0 on several populations, 0.9345 on the arylamide population, and 0.7184 on the sulfur-cage population. These are molecule-level text counters, not aromatic atom fractions, ring feasibility, or molecular conformations. The outputs range from recognizable indole carboxamides and aryl cyclic amines to heavily bridged N/O frameworks, long sulfur/oxygen side chains, and multiply bonded sulfur cages. Mean SMILES lengths range from 46.9 to 69.0; the main problem is not a population of trivial fragments or universally giant repeated assemblies. Rather, much of the visible variety changes decoration or connectivity within seed-specific complex families. Explicit charge and tetrahedral stereolabel rates are zero, despite potentially basic amines and stereogenic carbon or sulfur connectivity. Some current chemistry differs meaningfully from the parent, especially the sulfur-free aryl-amine leader, while other leading structures and entire chemical trajectories are unchanged. Apparent synthetic plausibility remains questionable and overall drug likeness weak because useful recognizable groups coexist with strained rings, unusual sulfur valence, reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds, and undefined stereochemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The compact leaders carry aromatic rings and amide or ketone carbonyls, but they separate into chemically different families. The best combines an alkyl-substituted unsaturated sulfur/nitrogen ring system, a primary carboxamide, and an acylated nitrogen bridging adjacent benzene carbons. That last unit is a strained benzene-fused small nitrogen ring, not an ordinary anilide. Related leaders retain the same constrained amide nitrogen with benzothiophene, aminomethoxy, or chloromethyl substitution. A more conventional ethoxy/methyl/thiol-substituted indole carboxanilide is also near the top. The final seed instead favors pyridylmethyl ketones attached to unusual sulfur-containing unsaturated rings and a cyclobutadiene-like small ring. Ring presence is 1.0 and aromatic presence 0.9345, with mean SMILES length 46.9; ring abundance coexists with substantial chemical strain.
liabilities: The acylated nitrogen bridging adjacent aromatic carbons creates severe small-ring geometry concerns.
Multiply bonded ring sulfur with additional substituents should not be read as ordinary thiophene or terminal thiocarbonyl chemistry.
Late cyclobutadiene-like rings are highly strained, and several related products also contain N-N or N-O bonds.
Thiol and chloromethyl decorations add reactivity concerns without a consistent local score advantage.
missing_features: Ordinary amide-nitrogen and ring alternatives retaining the leading carbonyl and aromatic arrangement are not established within the strongest strained-amide series.
Stable sulfur bonding and less strained fusion patterns are underrepresented around the late pyridyl ketones.
Chemically credible matched alternatives linking the conventional indole family to the higher-scoring unusual topology are absent.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The unusual sulfur/strained-amide leader scores 0.425403, versus 0.404974 after adding a thiol to its benzene ring and 0.385223 after adding a hydroxyl group there. Thus those extra donor groups do not improve this local series. The conventional indole carboxanilide reaches 0.399050, above the initial methoxy-rich fluorophenyl indole amide at 0.305105; high scores do not require the strained nitrogen ring. Low optimizer molecules remain substantial: a reduced, N-O-containing arylamide with a difficult heteroaryl substituent scores 0.030640, and replacing the pyridyl region of a 0.390279 ketone family with an expanded nonaromatic nitrogen ring gives 0.031675. The observed association is with the intact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement rather than ring count alone. The current seed-0 maximum exceeds the parent's 0.396663, while the conventional seed-1 leader and its supplied chemical trajectory are unchanged. The current seed-2 maximum is below the parent's 0.410039 and replaces N-chloro arylamide chemistry with a different strained sulfur/ketone family.

per_task.generated_character: The dominant leading family is relatively large and flexible: a substituted chlorophenyl imine is connected through a fluorinated amino-bearing carbon to a nitrogen-rich fused carbonyl/thione ring system. An extended chain contains successive sulfur/oxygen connections, acetal-like centres, and a terminal chlorinated group; a multiply bonded, additionally substituted sulfur links it back toward the heterocycle. Some leaders replace an N-methyl group with direct N-bromination. Another current seed produces compact, extensively connected aza/oxygen rings with unusual sulfur triple bonding and cumulated nitrogen/carbon unsaturation. Late seed-2 molecules contain aromatic diones, sulfenyl bromides, thioether-rich branches, and unsaturated side chains. Aromatic and ring presence are both 1.0; mean SMILES length is 68.3 and maximum 95. These are complex complete molecules, with difficult stability and synthesis questions rather than missing ring content.
liabilities: Direct nitrogen-bromine and sulfur-bromine bonds are reactive functionalities, distinct from ordinary carbon-bound halogen substitution.
The additionally substituted carbon-sulfur multiple bonds and sulfur triple-bond motifs are chemically unusual.
Long mixed oxygen/sulfur chains and imine connections introduce potential hydrolytic or oxidative liabilities and many conformational choices.
The cumulated-double-bond token rate of 0.0874 supports a visible population of unusual unsaturated connections, but does not establish their stability.
missing_features: Matched stable replacements for the multiply bonded sulfur connections and direct N-bromination are not established around the leading architecture.
Shorter, less labile side chains preserving the main aryl/heterocarbonyl relationship are insufficiently represented.
Independent ordinary heteroaromatic frameworks with the same functional-group relationships are underrepresented relative to complex local rearrangements.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading sulfur-rich, N-brominated structure scores 0.616171 and is exactly the parent's seed-0 leader; that entire supplied chemical trajectory is unchanged. A group at 0.615507 includes extension of an aryl ethyl group to propyl, extension of a sulfur-bound methyl to ethyl, and a matched replacement of N-methyl by N-bromo. The score therefore provides no local evidence that N-bromination or those chain extensions are necessary. Low optimizer examples retain complete aryl/carbonyl scaffolds at 0.526082-0.531030, versus the initial aryl dione at 0.548381. The association is with detailed heteroatom and connecting-group arrangements, not simply having more heteroaromatic rings. The current seed-1 maximum is 0.606300 versus the parent's 0.590648, with more compact but chemically unusual fused-ring/sulfur chemistry; the current seed-2 maximum is 0.589214 versus the parent's 0.609218 and carries more sulfur-rich connections. These opposing chemical changes do not establish a universal benefit from sulfur accumulation.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest current family is sulfur-free and consists of dichlorophenyl and methoxyphenyl groups connected through an enamine-substituted azetidine, an imine, and a substituted carbon carrying aminomethyl and aziridine-containing groups. A phenolic hydroxyl is present in most leaders. These molecules contain several potentially basic nitrogens, with substantially more recognizable aryl-amine connectivity than the sulfur-rich cages seen elsewhere, but the aziridine is strained and potentially reactive, while imine/enamine stability remains unresolved. Other seeds retain highly bridged aromatic amine structures and unusual sulfur/nitrogen rings. Aromatic and ring presence are 1.0, halogen presence is 0.9966, and mean SMILES length is 69.0. Neutral SMILES do not mean these amines lack ionization.
liabilities: Aziridine strain and possible ring-opening reactivity remain even after the leading series removes unusual sulfur.
Imine and enamine groups can be chemically labile; the supplied scores do not establish solution stability.
Other high-scoring or final molecules still use multiply bonded sulfur, sulfur-rich cages, and strongly constrained ring connections.
Several potentially basic sites and stereogenic centres are represented without charge-state or stereochemical specification.
missing_features: Ordinary, less reactive ring replacements retaining the spacing of the leading aziridine-containing amine centres are absent from the cited top series.
Stable alternatives to imine and enamine connections have not been demonstrated while retaining the useful aryl/amine arrangement.
Defined stereoisomers of the substituted azetidine and central carbon connectivity are missing.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Inserting a methylene between the substituted central carbon and aziridine nitrogen gives the best score, 0.987877, versus 0.984295 for the directly connected aziridine. Removing the phenolic hydroxyl from the latter gives 0.979751. Replacing its aminomethyl group with nitrile gives 0.943733. These local comparisons support the assembled aryl/amine geometry and accessible amine functionality, without identifying a unique required ring. Early biaryl carboxylic acid, amide, and N-sulfonyl cyclic-amine molecules score only 0.007468-0.011876; many rings and nitrogens alone are insufficient. The current seed-0 maximum exceeds the parent's 0.885624 and replaces its multiply bonded sulfur/thione family with a sulfur-free one, a concrete improvement in the recognizability of the chemistry. The current seed-1 maximum is lower than the parent's, and the seed-2 maximum remains 0.914814 in the same sulfur-rich family. High overall scores therefore coexist with unresolved liabilities and different chemical outcomes across seeds.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are compact but highly bridged N/O polycycles. They combine an alkyl-substituted pyridine, a phenyl or phenol group, a partly saturated carbonyl-containing nitrogen ring, and an N-O bridge. Related structures insert N-N or O-O connections or adjust ring atoms and substituents. Their ring sizes are not uniformly tiny, but the overlapping bridges impose difficult spatial and synthetic constraints. Late seed-2 molecules add sulfur-rich bridges, a sulfinic-acid substituent, N-hydroxyl/hydrazine connectivity, and more expanded carbonyl-containing rings. Aromatic and ring presence are 1.0, halogen presence is 0.2839, and mean SMILES length is 61.7. This is abundant aromatic and cyclic carbonyl chemistry with poor representation of simple, readily interpretable alternatives.
liabilities: Complex overlapping N/O bridges make a feasible synthesis and accessible conformation uncertain despite moderate overall size.
Peroxide and direct oxygen-halogen connections appear in related or low-scoring products.
Late sulfur-rich structures combine unusual sulfur valence with hydroxylamine/hydrazine-like bonds.
Adding polar groups or more ring connections yields little supplied-score movement within the leading family.
missing_features: Less bridged architectures preserving the aryl, pyridyl, and carbonyl relationships are insufficiently represented among the leaders.
Stable oxygen and nitrogen connections replacing O-O, N-O, or N-N bridges have not been explored in a complete matched series.
Stereochemically specified versions of the saturated bridge connections are absent.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The phenol-containing N/O-bridged leader scores 0.210745 and is exactly the parent's leader; the whole seed-0 molecular/score trajectory is unchanged. Related nitrogen-versus-carbon connecting-group variants tie at 0.207758. Adding an oxygen to make an O-O-containing bridge lowers a closely related score to 0.206478, providing no evidence that the peroxide connection is useful. Early opened carbonyl/urea side-chain structures score 0.124680 and 0.126398, below the compact bridged family, but the bridge complexity itself is not isolated by those comparisons. A later O-F/peroxide/halogenated-chain molecule is also low at 0.130264, so additional heteroatoms and reactive bonds do not solve the limited score region. All seed maxima remain the parent's maxima. New late seed-2 sulfur-rich structures score roughly 0.158603-0.184191 and do not exceed the earlier 0.201856 carbonyl-rich structure.

per_task.generated_character: The highest-scoring molecules are densely fused and bridged sulfur-rich cages, containing unusual multiply bonded sulfur atoms, sulfur-sulfur connections, carbonyl/NH heterocycles, and fluorinated carbon substituents. The best includes a small carbon ring with exocyclic unsaturation embedded in the cage and a fluorinated hydroxyl-bearing carbon attached through a thioether. Other seeds yield similarly congested sulfur frameworks with acyl fluoride, aldehyde, N-F, or acyl-S-Cl functionality. Many structures have little ordinary aromatic surface beyond a retained nitrogen/carbonyl region; aromatic-token presence is 0.7184 while ring presence remains 1.0. Mean SMILES length is 62.8. Their moderate size should not obscure the severe challenges posed by unusual sulfur bonding, ring fusion, stereochemistry, and reactive functionality.
liabilities: Multiply bonded, additionally substituted sulfur and bracketed SH within congested rings require substantial chemical scrutiny.
Small carbon rings with exocyclic unsaturation and repeated fusion constrain geometry and synthesis.
Acyl fluoride, aldehyde, N-F, and acyl-S-Cl groups introduce additional reactivity concerns in individual seed families.
Many potential carbon and sulfur stereochemical distinctions remain unspecified throughout the unchanged output.
missing_features: Comparably sized, conventionally bonded scaffolds retaining the useful carbonyl and fluorinated substituent relationships are absent from the cited high-scoring series.
Credible alternatives to the densely bridged sulfur framework are not demonstrated at similar supplied scores.
Stable substitutes for acyl fluoride, N-F, and other reactive terminal groups are incompletely represented.
Explicit stereochemical identities and accessible conformations of the polycyclic cages are unresolved.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The complete supplied molecular/score trajectories are identical to the parent's on every seed, including the 0.590353 sulfur-cage maximum. Closely related cage rearrangements score 0.557051 and 0.552707. A local carbonyl-to-imino replacement lowers a related structure from 0.519850 to 0.484404, supporting a particular carbonyl arrangement in that series. Other sulfur-rich cages with N-F or oxidized sulfur groups score around 1.05e-9 or 8.33e-9, so sulfur accumulation and fluorination alone do not explain the high scores. Early aryl dione derivatives are also very low, for example 7.59e-10 and 5.37e-8. Final cage changes range from 0.004200 for an acyl-S-Cl-containing structure to 0.448455 for a different, more compact aldehyde-containing cage; their topology and functionality change together. The observed gradient is sensitive to the detailed carbonyl, fluorinated-group, and ring arrangement, but supplies no evidence that these difficult sulfur valences are chemically necessary.

transferable_gaps.evidence: High-scoring outputs repeatedly contain carbon-sulfur multiple bonds at additionally substituted sulfur, bracketed SH embedded in rings, sulfur-sulfur bonds, and sulfur-rich cages. A stronger sulfur-free aryl-amine series and a near-leading conventional indole amide show that useful scores can coexist with more ordinary bonding.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve conventional sulfur bonding when producing complex ring and connecting-group chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make local replacement of unusual sulfur centres by conventionally bonded sulfur, carbon, nitrogen, or oxygen connections accessible while preserving surrounding substituent positions and approximate size. Use the current objective's feedback to determine which replacements retain useful chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited outputs include nitrogen bridges across adjacent aromatic carbons, cyclobutadiene-like rings, aziridine-containing amines, and highly overlapping N/O or sulfur cages. Ring-closure token presence is 1.0 throughout, so successful ring generation is already abundant while ordinary accessible topology is underrepresented.
transferable_gaps.gap: Geometric feasibility is not consistently maintained when rings are fused, bridged, or contracted.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide ring expansion, saturation, bridge opening, and alternative fusion connections that preserve the surrounding functional-group arrangement. Distinguish feasible ring geometry from the mere ability to write a valence-valid ring closure.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A matched N-methyl/N-bromo pair shares the supplied score 0.615507, while insertion of an O-O connection lowers a related score from 0.207758 to 0.206478. Other outputs carry O-F, S-Br, N-F, acyl fluoride, or acyl-S-Cl groups, including several very low-scoring structures.
transferable_gaps.gap: Reactive heteroatom-halogen and peroxide functionality is introduced without demonstrated local benefit.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support matched stable replacements or removal of these bonds while retaining the nearby scaffold and useful heteroatom placement. Avoid interpreting their presence in a high-scoring whole molecule as evidence that the reactive group is required.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest population has zero explicit tetrahedral stereolabel presence. The cited molecules include substituted saturated nitrogen rings, branched fluorinated carbon centres, and dense carbon/sulfur cages capable of distinct stereochemical arrangements.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereochemical identity is absent despite increasingly constrained and stereogenic output structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve existing stereochemical information through edits and expose valid local stereoisomers when new stereogenic connections arise. Couple stereochemical alternatives to geometrically credible structures and current score feedback, rather than assuming unspecified connectivity represents an accessible molecule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Many leaders differ only in side-chain length, heteroatom decoration, or bridge rearrangement, including exact score ties. Low-scoring molecules are already substantial aromatic/carbonyl structures, so merely generating rings or retaining molecular size does not fill the gap. More conventional aryl amides and sulfur-free aryl amines provide concrete starting chemistry for alternative connections.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output provides too few simple, independently connected alternatives to its complex seed-specific families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable matched changes to connecting groups, carbonyl placement, and aryl substitution, together with simplification of redundant bridges and labile side chains. Preserve the informative molecular core while exposing chemically distinct, synthetically credible ways to arrange its groups.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
